review_text_raw:
Love this game. In the same vein as films like 'Searching', you spend all of your time navigating a device (in this case a phone) in search of a missing person. Simulacra has more a horror tone than 'Searching', but for much of the game's runtime it's only lightly scary, with most of the suspense coming not from supernatural frights but from further unraveling the mystery by feeling like an amateur cybersleuth. 

There are definitely moments where it was frustrating trying to figure out where to go next, but the game generally does a good job of pointing you in the right direction through the use of hints given by the characters in the game. It all feels organic and never too forced. Multiple playthroughs will be needed to see all of the endings, but even just one playthrough will give every player a satisfying experience in the end. 

My few gripes with this game are that the actors aren't really that great in their performances, and for a game that I think is set in the US (at least that seems like the accent everyone is going for), the actor's accents waver quite often. This is obviously not a big budget production, so it's understandable that top shelf talent isn't within reach, but I would say that instead of trying to force a setting, just go with what's available around you. I don't feel that the US setting is necessary to tell this kind of story. I'd also like if there were some way to expedite replays of the game. Yes, if you do a second playthrough you can skip text much more quickly, but I'm thinking of something kinda like Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward. In that title there was a branching path menu you could pull up and jump exactly to the point where the story diverged. That would save so much time replaying up until the point where a critical decision was made. 

Conclusion:

Fun cyberdetective game told through a smartphone. Elements of horror, but nothing too overdone so that non-horror fans couldn't enjoy. Gameplay makes you do a fair amount of thinking, without too much handholding, so you feel a sense of accomplishment when you unearth another clue. Tons of easter eggs are there for those willing to look. Performances are not great here, but the voiced parts are minimal and don't interrupt the flow too often. 

Playtime: 4.4 hrs
100% completion
Played on Steam Deck (100% Compatible)

*Spoiler free*

Well, what can I say? Not at all what I expected from this kind of game. I expected to be a little bored. I expected it to feel repetitive. I expected to quit before the game was over. That's not what happened at all. 

The story was engaging to the point of a novel worthy "couldn't put it down" feel. I had to know what was going on and what would happen to the characters involved. Somehow it managed to create an incredible atmosphere that I would not have credited a game that takes place on a mobile phone as being capable of. 

Simulacra kept me guessing till the end. It also has replay value because your choices matter and there is more than one way for this game to end based on the choices you make. 

For the price it can't be faulted and I would have paid more. The best way to play this is on your mobile phone, but I played the first time on my PC and  found it just as immersive. 

This game will not treat you like a child and it will not hold your hand. You will have to think and you will have to figure things out.

review_text_raw: The acting in this game is atrocious. The characters are unpleasant and you aren't given nearly any choice as to whether you do as they say or not. The two characters you interact with for the first chunk of the game are both men who treat the disapearance of Anna as entertaining and a personal affront respectively, and your character gives them all the information they request without hesitation. The jumpscares and supernatural elements are dull and overplayed. Other games have used this genre to create engaging puzzles like figuring out someones password by reading through their texts and checking their photos. This game holds your hand through these things and straight up has other characters tell you what to do, ruining the immerison. Then they add more immerison breaking puzzles by scrambling the order of some texts and images on the phone that the player then has put in order. This is a boring puzzle and the revealed texts and images are usually unsatisfying.

review_text_raw:
Summary: For a horror/mystery/puzzle game, it is quite weak on each of the three elements. The least surprising mystery game I've played. Perhaps mainly because it blows its load from the start and spends the rest of the play time catching up with itself. Probably works better on mobile, as it seems made for a short attention span.

Pros:
- Basic concept is a cool commentary on social media and online dating
- A couple of surprising moments
- Some easter eggs and alternative paths give a bit of replay value

Cons:
- Storytelling is overstated and predictable
- Dialog is unconvincing, and I often didn't like my choices
- Game is linear and holds your hand almost the entire way. Some light puzzles, but otherwise no challenge, except unlocking a certain ending
- Acting is meh, supporting voice acting is mostly plain bad
- Annoying spelling errors are not always intentional

For examples of similar storytelling that really works: see Oxenfree and Doki Doki Literature Club.

review_text_raw:
This was certainly a unique idea for the game: figuring out what happened to the owner of the phone you picked up by going through the history of her chats and speaking to people on her contact list. The puzzles are intuitive and the game doesn't hold your hand in solving them, so its very satisfying when you get that "EUREKA!" moment as you remember a detail mentioned off-handledy in one of the documents you read hours later.

Yes, the gameplay is thrilling, but I wish it was attached to a more interesting plot. Anna's personal life amounts to standard relationship problems, which wouldn't be such a problem if the characters were more interesting. A troubled girl... her cheating boyfreiend... her supportive friends... and a jokester. All standard horror-movie players and despite games attempts to give them some depth, they just weren't all that engaging. 

There's also the obligatory twist ending. The game does good job building up the mystery and tension of what happened to Anna... but the resolution is rather silly. In general for a horror game its not particularly scary as it mostly relies on predictable jump scares.

Despite the basic premise, the game is quite lengthy (my first playthrough was over 4 houts long) and there's a a bit of replay value to it as some puzzles have several ways to solve depending on what plot choices you make.

7/10 (Mostly for the gameplay and presentation)

It's a neat little game for the price.

Really fun game!  I almost wish they forced you to dig on your own without as much hand holding.  I get why they guide you, and want to move the story forward, but I would have been fine without the objective list and task notification system.

Still - I appreciate that it split the difference between games like Her Story and a regular narrative.  Really good balance!
